name: Interior Strip & Deadener Removal
description: Taking the Gen 6 Camaro shell down to bare metal: all trim, seats, belts, carpet, headliner, SRS and asphalt sound deadener removed; open holes plugged.

components.name: Factory sound deadener / NVH material removal
components.description: Asphalt melt-sheet and spray deadener on floor, tunnel, and rear wheelhouses removed (dry ice or heat gun + scraper) to save weight and to give clean metal for cage plates, seat mounts and welding (deadener is also a fire hazard near welds).
components.location: Entire cabin floor pan, tunnel, footwells, rear seat area and trunk floor (x ≈ 0.7–3.6).

factory.name: GM asphalt-based melt sheets + foam NVH pads
factory.notes: Weight removed varies; typically tens of pounds on modern coupes (not verified for Camaro).

specs.Method: Dry ice + mallet (cleanest) or heat gun + scraper; finish with solvent
specs.Weight saved: Not verified – weigh what you remove

installNotes: Clean to bare metal only where plates/welds go; prime/seal exposed metal afterward.
inspection: Look for hidden rust/corrosion once exposed.

sources.title: NASA Speed News – Project Spec E30: building a roll cage

components.name: SRS / airbag system removal
components.description: Driver, passenger, knee, seat and roof-rail airbags, pretensioners and the sensing module are removed – airbags are incompatible with a race seat/harness/FHR and live inflators are dangerous during cage welding. Inflators must be handled and disposed of per hazardous-materials rules.
components.location: Steering wheel, IP, seats, roof rails, B-pillar pretensioners.

factory.name: GM SRS (front, knee, side, curtain airbags; belt pretensioners)
factory.notes: Disconnect battery and wait per GM SI before handling.

installNotes: Disconnect battery and wait the GM-specified time before unplugging modules.
Remove curtain airbags BEFORE cutting/welding near roof rails.
ECU/BCM may need reprogramming to suppress SRS fault messages (electrical team).
inspection: Confirm no live inflators remain in shell.

sources.title: NASA Speed News – Project Spec E30: building a roll cage

components.name: Seats, carpet, headliner, rear seat & trim deleted
components.description: Factory front/rear seats, carpet, headliner, pillar trims, door trims, rear seat and trunk liners removed. Keep the parts list of what was removed (and weights) for class weight calculations.
installNotes: Bag and label factory fasteners you may reuse (seat studs, belt anchor bolts).

sources.title: NASA Speed News – Project Spec E30: building a roll cage

components.name: Floor/body hole plugs
components.description: Rubber or steel plugs (or welded patches) closing drain holes, unused harness pass-throughs, and seat-belt anchor holes after stripping – keeps water, exhaust fumes and fire out of the cockpit.
components.location: Floor pan, firewall, rear wheelhouses, trunk floor.

specs.Types: Rubber/EPDM press-in plugs; steel plug + seam sealer; weld-in patch

installNotes: Weld-patch holes near the fuel cell and firewall rather than rubber plugs.
inspection: Check plugs still present after undercar strikes.

sources.title: SCCA Time Trials – Full Safety Rules
